llm_response.content:
Empirical Research Plan: 2003 Los Angeles MTA Strike and Freeway Congestion  

=========================================================================  

1. Identification Strategy  
--------------------------  
Preferred design: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-study extension (dynamic DiD).

Why it fits  
• Sharp, plausibly exogenous “treatment” on 14 Oct 2003: a 100 % shutdown of bus/rail.  
• Rich panel (detector × hour) lets us difference both over time and across detectors in areas that did versus did not lose transit.  
• Controls (Orange & Ventura county freeways, plus the same LA detectors in 2004) provide untreated outcomes that should share weather, seasonality, gasoline prices, etc.  
• Event-study coefficients allow us to check pre-trend credibility and trace daily/hourly adjustment paths.

2. Treatment and Control  
------------------------  
Treatment variable  
  Treat_i = 1 for loop detector i located on a Los-Angeles-County freeway; 0 otherwise.  

Control groups (two are used)  
  A. Primary: Detectors on freeways in Orange & Ventura counties (no MTA service loss).  
  B. Placebo: The *same* LA-county detectors observed in 2004 (Oct 14 ± 28 days) when no strike occurred.  

Treatment timing  
  Post_t = 1 for hours ≥ 00:00 on Tuesday 14 Oct 2003 and ≤ 23:59 on Monday 17 Nov 2003 (inclusive).  
  We exclude the ramp-up week (18–24 Nov) in main spec; include it in robustness.  

Event-study clock  
  k = −28,…,+35 where k = 0 is 14 Oct 2003.  

Running variable / cutoff  
  Not applicable (no RDD).

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of a transit strike, congestion on LA and control freeways would have evolved similarly through autumn 2003.  
  Plausibility: Neighboring counties share weather, economic conditions, commuter patterns; we also verify with 2002–2004 pre-strike windows.  

A2. No spillovers to control roads: The strike should not materially change flows on Orange/Ventura freeways.  
  Plausibility: Most MTA riders start/end inside LA County; freeways in adjacent counties are > 10 mi from most bus/rail routes. We will check controls for detectable breaks.  

A3. Exogeneity of strike timing: The expiration of a court injunction created an abrupt, largely unanticipated stoppage.  
  Plausibility: News coverage shows no schedule of contingency service, and bargaining had broken down suddenly the evening before.  

A4. Stable detector sample / measurement: Loop detectors stay functional throughout.  
  Plausibility: PeMS flags missing or faulty detectors; we drop those with < 90 % uptime.  

4. Main Threats and Mitigation  
------------------------------  
T1. Concurrent shocks (e.g., wild-fires, weather, gasoline price spike).  
  Fix: Include county-by-day fixed effects for temperature, precipitation, AQI, and CalFire incident dummies; verify in placebo year.  

T2. Spillover congestion on control roads via diverted drivers from LA.  
  Fix:  
   • Exclude Orange/Ventura detectors within 3 mi of county border.  
   • Estimate an “intensity” model using distance-to-LA border interacted with Post to test for gradient effects.  

T3. Endogenous road closures / construction reacting to strike.  
  Fix: Obtain Caltrans lane-closure logs; drop detector-hours with active closures; interact closure dummy with Treat to show results robustness.  

5. R Code Outline  
-----------------  
```r
# 0. Libraries ------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)      # fast high-dimensional DiD
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data ------------------------------------------------------------
det <- fread("pems_hourly_2003.csv")   # assumes columns: detector_id, county,
                                       # date_time (POSIXct), speed, delay,
                                       # flow, occ
det[, date := as.Date(date_time)]
det[, hour := hour(date_time)]

# 2. Keep weekday peak hours ---------------------------------------------
det <- det[weekdays(date) %in% c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday") &
             ((hour>=7 & hour<10) | (hour>=14 & hour<20))]

# 3. Construct treatment / timing ----------------------------------------
strike_start <- as.Date("2003-10-14")
strike_end   <- as.Date("2003-11-17")
window_start <- strike_start - 28
window_end   <- strike_start + 28

sample <- det[date %between% c(window_start,window_end)]

sample[, treat := as.integer(county=="LosAngeles")]
sample[, post  := as.integer(date>=strike_start & date<=strike_end)]
sample[, rel_day := as.integer(date - strike_start)]

# 4. Baseline DiD ---------------------------------------------------------
did1 <- feols(speed ~ treat*post |
                detector_id + date + hour,  # two-way FE + hour-of-day
              data = sample, vcov = "cluster~detector_id+date")
etable(did1)

# 5. Event study (Sun & Abraham) ------------------------------------------
# create sunab terms: interact treat with relative time
sample[, rel_grp := fifelse(rel_day < -7, -7,
                     fifelse(rel_day > 35, 35, rel_day))]
es <- feols(speed ~ sunab(treat, rel_grp) |
              detector_id + date + hour,
            data = sample, vcov = "cluster~detector_id+date")
iplot(es, ref.line = 0, xlab="Days relative to strike", ylab="Δ Speed (mph)")

# 6. Robustness: placebo year (2004) --------------------------------------
pl2004 <- fread("pems_hourly_2004.csv")
pl2004[, date := as.Date(date_time)]
pl2004[, hour := hour(date_time)]
pl2004 <- pl2004[weekdays(date) %in% c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday") &
                   ((hour>=7 & hour<10)|(hour>=14 & hour<20))]
pl2004 <- pl2004[date %between% c(as.Date("2004-10-14")-28, as.Date("2004-10-14")+28)]
pl2004[, treat := as.integer(county=="LosAngeles")]
pl2004[, post  := as.integer(date>=as.Date("2004-10-14") &
                              date<=as.Date("2004-11-17"))]

placebo <- feols(speed ~ treat*post | detector_id + date + hour,
                 data = pl2004, vcov="cluster~detector_id+date")
etable(placebo)
```

6. Expected Results  
-------------------  
Theory: With 1.3 million daily transit boardings removed, a subset shifts to cars, raising vehicle-miles-traveled (VMT) and congestion. So:

• Average peak-period speed on LA freeways should *fall*.  
• Ballpark: Suppose 10 % of bus/rail riders switch to freeways during peaks (≈ 65 k people). Even a 2–3 % traffic increase can drop speeds by 5–10 %. I expect −3 to −5 mph on average and delay ↑ 0.2–0.4 min/mi relative to controls.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)  
-------------------------------------------  
C1. No differential pre-trends?  1 (checked with event study)  
C2. Exogenous treatment timing?  1  
C3. No contemporaneous policy shocks? 0.5 (wild-fire risk, but controlled)  
C4. Stable composition of units? 0.5 (detector outages possible; we screen)  
C5. No spillovers/contamination? 0.5 (may spill into control counties; tested)  

Total ≈ 3.5 / 5 ⇒ credible but not bullet-proof.

=========================================================================
